Social posts

Short posts for X, Bluesky, Mastodon, and LinkedIn, plus a four-post thread. Attach the image named in each section and use the alt text from screenshots.md. Character counts below include the text as written; check them again if you edit before posting.

X and Bluesky

X allows 280 characters and Bluesky allows 300. This post fits both.

Image: ../assets/screenshots/html-report.webp

Your update bot says a newer version exists. Offing tells you what is end-of-life, where this repo uses it, and which source backs the claim. Local-first, offline scans, no account.

npx @velella/offing scan .

https://github.com/velella-sh/offing

Character count: 259.

Mastodon

Mastodon's default limit is 500 characters, though some instances raise or lower it. This post fits the default.

Image: ../assets/screenshots/treemap.webp

Offing is a local-first CLI that finds end-of-life runtimes, deprecated packages, and retired GitHub Actions at the exact file and line. Every finding has severity, a replacement, and an authoritative source. Scans are offline, need no account, and never execute repository code. It also runs as a local MCP server, a GitHub Action, and an Agent Skill, with a baseline so CI gates new findings, not accepted ones.

npx @velella/offing scan .

https://github.com/velella-sh/offing

Character count: 491.

Alt text: Treemap of Offing findings by file, sized by severity-weighted finding count and colored by the highest severity in each file.

LinkedIn

Image: ../assets/screenshots/job-summary.webp

Most dependency tools answer one question: is there a newer version? Offing answers another: what in this repository is about to stop working, where is it used, and what evidence says so?

Offing is a local-first CLI that finds end-of-life runtimes, deprecated packages, and retired GitHub Actions at the exact file and line. Each finding carries severity, a replacement, an authoritative source, and migration context for a human or coding agent. Scans make no network requests, need no account, and never execute repository code.

It runs as a CLI, a local MCP server, a GitHub Action, and an Agent Skill. A baseline accepts known findings with an owner, reason, and expiry, so CI gates new findings, not accepted ones.

npx @velella/offing scan .

https://github.com/velella-sh/offing

Alt text: GitHub Actions job summary from Offing showing two high and one medium finding, with file locations and evidence labels.

Thread

Use the thread when one post is not enough. Each post fits X and Bluesky limits.

Post 1

Dependency bots tell you a newer version exists. They rarely tell you which removal will break your repo, where it is used, or what evidence backs the claim. I maintain Offing, a local-first CLI for that question. 1/4

Post 2

Scan a checkout and get every end-of-life runtime, deprecated package, and retired GitHub Action at the exact file and line, with severity, replacement, source, and migration context. 2/4

Image for post 2: ../assets/screenshots/html-report.webp with the same alt text as the X post.

Post 3

Scans are offline, need no account, and never execute repository code. Baseline known findings; gate CI only on new ones. GitHub Action, GitLab component, local MCP server, and Agent Skill. 3/4

Post 4

Try: npx @velella/offing scan . Then tell me which lifecycle risks your current tooling misses. https://github.com/velella-sh/offing 4/4

Where to post

  • X and Bluesky: use the single post first. Quote-post or reply with the thread only if there is interest.
  • Mastodon: use the Mastodon post on a technology or open-source instance. Add the image's alt text; do not rely on the platform to generate it.
  • LinkedIn: use the LinkedIn post and one image. Keep the first two lines readable before the "see more" fold; they already carry the hook.
  • Dev communities: if a community reposts the thread, link to the original instead of reposting the same text.

Notes

  • Disclose that you maintain the project where the platform or community requires it, and do not ask for upvotes, boosts, or likes.
  • Do not add engagement bait, emojis, or hashtag blocks. One or two relevant hashtags on LinkedIn are enough if you want them.
  • Keep the no-data and scope language out of the short posts only because there is no room; the linked documentation carries the limits.
